summary.title: Beej's Guide to Network Programming
summary.one_liner: A free guide to writing networked C programs with the Berkeley sockets API, aimed at readers who already know C or C++.
keywords: how to write network code in c
takeaways: The guide teaches network programming with Internet sockets, also called sockets programming.
The sockets API originated with Berkeley and is available on Unix, Linux and Windows.
Prior knowledge of C or C++ is assumed; the guide is meant to get readers started with the API.
The guide is available as HTML and PDF in several paper sizes and colour styles, and as a GitHub clone with a Makefile.
summary.summary: This is Beej's free how-to guide on network programming with Internet sockets, often called sockets programming. It introduces the Berkeley sockets API, which has been ported to Unix, Linux and Windows, and assumes the reader knows some C or C++. The page itself is mostly navigation and download links: HTML and PDF versions in US Letter and A4, one- and two-sided, colour and black-and-white, plus translations into several languages. The source can be cloned from GitHub and built by following its README.
